paragraphs.text: A **cash-secured put** is a short put position in which the writer sets aside enough cash to buy the shares at the strike price if the put is assigned, collects the premium up front, and accepts the obligation to buy 100 shares per contract at the strike any time before expiration [S1]. A **naked put** on margin is the same contract, but the broker holds only a margin requirement, a fraction of the purchase price computed under exchange and FINRA minimum rules, leaving the rest of the buying power free [S6].

The screen allocated {{allocation.csp_pct|pct}} of the strategy budget to cash-secured puts, {{allocation.leaps_pct|pct}} to LEAPS and {{allocation.cash_pct|pct}} to cash, with a tilt of {{allocation.tilt}}. The market regime label was {{regime.label}}, with a VIX of {{regime.vix}}.

**LEAPS** (Long-term Equity AnticiPation Securities) are listed options with more than a year until expiration that trade and settle like shorter options [S3]. A **poor man's covered call** is a two-leg position: a long, deep in-the-money LEAPS call and a short, near-term, out-of-the-money call on the same stock, formally a long call diagonal spread with different strikes and different expirations [S5]. Every option premium splits into **intrinsic value**, the amount by which the option is in the money, and **extrinsic value**, or time value, everything else; at expiration extrinsic value is always zero [S4].
